awd_titl_txt: Conference Support for the Super Dual Auroral Radar Network Workshop 2025; Roanoke, Virginia; June 2025
awd_abstract_narration:
The Super Dual Auroral Radar Network (SuperDARN) Workshop 2025 will be held in Roanoke, Virginia, in June 2025. SuperDARN is an international network of radars operated by science and engineering institutions located in more than a dozen countries worldwide. The network consists of over 30 low-power radars extending across three latitudinal tiers from mid-latitudes, through the auroral zone, and into the polar cap, in both hemispheres. Four US universities, with Virginia Tech as lead institution, form a US SuperDARN collaboration that is funded by NSF. The SuperDARN array provides remotely sensed observations of various geophysical phenomena in the Earth’s upper atmosphere. These observations have contributed to significant advances in geospace research and plasma physics. The annual workshop of the SuperDARN collaboration is an opportunity for SuperDARN researchers to coordinate on scheduling and operations, new technical developments, software and analysis, and scientific collaborations. The SuperDARN Workshop serves as an excellent platform to exchange ideas about recent trends and developments in SuperDARN operations and research. The annual SuperDARN Workshop has a track record of fostering strong international collaborations with broad scientific and engineering impact, not only within the SuperDARN community, but across the entire space science discipline.

The Workshop proceeds as a conference with a sizable but manageable number of attendees. The sessions are held over a one-week period. The scientific sessions take place in a single conference room and are ordered thematically, for example ‘large-scale plasma convection’, ‘ultra-low frequency waves’, ‘atmospheric gravity waves and traveling ionospheric disturbances’, etc. The SuperDARN collaboration is managed at the highest level by the SuperDARN Executive Council and working groups commissioned on an ongoing basis to manage tasks such as scheduling, software development, data distribution, and coordination with outside groups of researchers such as satellite mission teams. Attendance by graduate students and early career researchers will be supported. Graduate students get exposure to both the operational and scientific aspects of SuperDARN, as well as to the broad range of research activities carried out by the global SuperDARN community. The Workshop also serves as an excellent platform for both students and early-career researchers to develop collaborations, work on new research avenues, and explore new exciting career paths.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The annual workshop of the Super Dual Auroral Network (SuperDARN) collaboration is an opportunity for researchers working on SuperDARN radars as well as those using the data products to meet and discuss research updates. The agenda typically includes coordinating on scheduling and operations, new technical developments, software and analysis, and scientific collaborations, both within the collaboration and with scientists from the broader research community. We requested support to hold the 2025 Workshop in Roanoke, Virginia hosted by the Virginia Tech SuperDARN group.  The main objective was to facilitate research on themes of interest to the space science research community generally and to the Geospace Cluster section of NSF in particular. Another objective was to increase the impact of the Workshop by boosting attendance, especially that of early career researchers and invited attendees, by subsidizing registration fees. Several different scientific themes and research topics that are of interest to the space science community were expected to be discussed at the workshop. These include High Frequency (HF) radio wave propagation analysis, space weather, magnetospheric dynamics, and response to changes in the solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field (IMF), magnetospheric storms and substorms, Traveling Ionospheric Disturbances (TIDs), etc.

The 2025 SuperDARN workshop was successfully held in Roanoke, Va between June 2-6, 2025.  A total of 52 attendees from 9 countries and 27 institutions participated in the workshop. The registration fee for some early career researchers was waived to support their participation. The Organizing Committee hosted multiple sessions covering a broad range of topics that not only focused on SuperDARN operations, but also were of interest to the broader space science community. These included sessions on Geomagnetic Storms & Modeling, Magnetosphere-Ionosphere (MI) coupling, Traveling Ionospheric Disturbance (TIDs) and neutral atmosphere, Ionospheric Physics and Irregularities, etc. More than 65 talks and posters were presented at the workshop, covering these science themes. Other activities included evening meetings of the SuperDARN PI Executive Council (to deliberate on overall policy and strategic planning)  and of SuperDARN Working Groups (to review technical issues related to the operation of the collaboration).

Early career researchers and students were provided an opportunity to present their research, foster new collaborations, and learn about SuperDARN. The workshop has increased community interest in general. Several US researchers, not directly affiliated with SuperDARN, were invited to participate in the workshop. This increased their awareness about recent upgrades to SuperDARN radars and the new capabilities of the radars in general.

A dedicated website for the workshop was created which include all the key details: http://vt.superdarn.org/workshop/
